title: Kenai for Android · functional replica of today's app
brief: A live, clickable copy of the real Kenai Android app as it is today (English texts from strings.xml, the current dark look from Tokens.DARK), not a new direction. Every screen is reachable (Pairing, Scan, Home, Chat, Settings, History, Gallery, Diagnostics, Licences, Session details), the approval, question and diff sheets work with a simulated fingerprint, and the demo loop of DemoLink.kt runs every 2.5 s. Three modes: Not paired, Demo mode, and Paired with fake data for what the desktop does not serve yet (chat, question options, diffs, plan usage, services, session details). On the right, an Android home screen (10 x 6 cells) shows the 9 Kenai widgets at the grid size of their widget_info (Big status 4x4, All your agents 4x3, Agents summary 3x2, One-line status 4x1, At a glance, Approvals waiting, Plan usage and Finished today 2x2, Agents' mood 1x1), redrawn from window.kenai on every change with the texts and rules of core/Glance.kt and core/WidgetData.kt, so they follow the 8-step loop, the not-connected states and the fake plan usage; every card and button opens the phone like the real PendingIntents, and a 'Widgets: dark / light' switch shows their day/night look. A 'View' control in the toolbar adds three more views beside the same live phone, all driven by its state: Screens, a jump rail that puts the phone on every screen, sheet and state (by demo step, by agent surface, by Chat, Settings and link state) and holds it there; Over other apps, the island pill of ui/IslandOverlay.kt drawn from core/IslandGeometry.kt (pure black, flush with the top edge, concave 14 px ears, working strip 240 wide and cards 308, below-corner radius 14 or 22, heights 28+52 / 28+96 / 28+168) over a fake messages app, with core/IslandPlan.active's pick (request, then question, then a working agent) or a manual Kind, OverlayPolicy's three blockers with their exact words, the 600 ms tap guard, Deny acting on the live phone, Allow opening its approval and a body tap opening Home; and Notifications, the heads-up, the pulled-down shade and the lock screen of app/Notifications.kt: one loud approval ('Claude Code needs your approval' + 'Wants to run a command', Deny and Review request, no Allow, a 2:00 chronometer counting down live), the quiet link and state notifications with their channel, group and public lock-screen versions, and the heads-up (approvals_v3, HIGH, vibration 0,500,150,500) against the quiet channel (approvals_quiet, LOW) that leaves only the pill as the alert.

artboards.title: Kenai today · live phone
artboards.tradeoff: Faithful to today's app and fully clickable, so it is the baseline to compare the light theme, Spanish and the new features against; the character is drawn approximately (the clay engine is not ported) and Android's own screens (fingerprint, permissions, settings) are stand-ins. The widgets are HTML, not RemoteViews bitmaps: same layouts, sizes, colours and texts, but Kenai is the same approximate clay drawing (still, with its glow), the launcher grid is a fixed 94 x 106 dp cell, and Finished today counts only in Paired mode, as the real app does. The three new views are drawings too, and say so in place: the island is HTML and CSS placed with IslandGeometry.kt's numbers and told what to show by the same rules (IslandPlan, IslandTimeline, OverlayPolicy), not a real overlay window and not the Compose code; its flash kinds are held 10 s and then retract in 340 ms, as the Kotlin does, but a real phone also decides with the cutout and the screen state. The notifications and the lock screen are HTML stand-ins for Android's own surfaces: there are no RemoteViews, the shade and the lock screen are not the system UI, and the fake messages app under the island is invented. The strings, the channel names, the group rule (no summary, so no «2» bundle), the actions and the countdown are the app's own.
